control_flow: stopAtWall: if the right obstacle sensor sees something, turn right 90°; else call followLine.
followLine: if the line tracker sees black, curve left; else curve right.

likely_intent.description: Stop before the wall without driving into it.

decision_points.condition: the right obstacle sensor sees a wall

branches.outcome: a wall is seen on the right: it turns right 90°
no wall is seen on the right: it calls followLine
the line tracker sees black: it curves left
the line tracker does not see black: it curves right

input_dimensions.dimension: where the robot starts relative to the line

equivalence_classes: a wall across the line ahead, in front of the right sensor
input_dimensions.dimension: what is ahead on its right
where the robot starts relative to the line
what is ahead on its right

scenarios.coded_response: It turns right 90° at 30 %, then loops and follows the line again.
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot follows a line in bright light, and a wall stands across the line ahead, in front of its right sensor.
scenarios.trigger: The robot comes close enough for its right obstacle sensor to see the wall.
scenarios.title: Stops at a wall
assumptions: The wall stands across the line the robot follows, so its right sensor can see it.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It stops before the wall without bumping into it, and stays there.

scenarios.coded_response: It curves left when the line tracker sees black and right when it does not.
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot stands on a line in bright light, with nothing in front of its right obstacle sensor.
scenarios.trigger: The line tracker sees black or the floor while the program runs.
scenarios.title: Follows the line when no wall is on its right
assumptions: You only said what should happen at the wall, not what the robot should do along the line.

uncertainties: You said stop at the wall, but the program has no stop block: when its right sensor sees a wall it turns right 90°.
The program reads only the right obstacle sensor, not the one ahead: the wall must stand in front of its right side.
You didn't say what the robot should do when no wall is in front of it.

outcomes.words: the condition doesn't hold: the else part runs
the condition doesn't hold: the else part runs

tests.name: Stops before the wall
tests.scenario: Given the robot follows the line at A, when a wall stands across the line ahead, then the robot stops in front of the wall without bumping into it and stays there.

equivalence_partitions.selected_realization: A, on the line's first point, facing along it
equivalence_partitions.dimension: where the robot starts relative to the line

equivalence_partitions.selected_realization: the Wall t2 across the line, 30 cm ahead of A and spanning the robot's whole front
equivalence_partitions.dimension: what is ahead on its right
equivalence_partitions.class: a wall across the line ahead, in front of the right sensor

expected_results: It follows the line and stops in front of the wall, without bumping into it.

postconditions.description: During the whole run, the robot never bumps into the wall.
Whenever the wall is ahead, the robot stands still.
At the end, the robot stands just before the wall.

assumptions: The wall stands across the line the robot follows, so its right sensor can see it.

tests.reason: Stopping at the wall is what you said.
